subject: MSA + Order Form: DPA execution playbook and SCCs / TIA coordination
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@cardiopath.com>, legal@cardiopath.com
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, monica.patel@redwood.ai, aditya.rao@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: MSA + Order Form: DPA execution playbook and SCCs / TIA coordination

Hi Elena / CardioPath legal team,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Attached is our proposed DPA redline (Redwood_DPA_redline_v3.docx) that aligns with the SCCs we discussed and includes a Transfer Impact Addendum (TIA) placeholder. High-level asks from our side:

- Confirm preferred role mapping (Controller / Processor / Joint Controller) for the Order Form scope. We currently map Redwood as Processor for inference and embeddings, controller for certain customer-managed datasets — see section 2.1.
- Confirm whether your legal team needs an explicit subprocessor list or an exhibit that references our published subprocessor page (we can provide an up-to-date export).
- Review the TIA mitigations in the draft and let us know if you need additional contractual safeguards (e.g., supplementary technical controls, KMS requirements, or local auditing rights).
- Deadline: commercial sponsor needs an executed DPA by EOD 2026-12-07 to meet procurement gating. Can you confirm whether that timeline works?

Key attachments: Redwood_DPA_redline_v3.docx (redlines inline), OrderForm-commercial-markup.xlsx (commercial items that may change liability caps).

If it helps, Laura (cc) can run a quick side-by-side with our MSA redlines and surface any misalignments across exhibits. Monica will gather evidence for transfer mitigations (SOC 2 scope, data residency controls). Aditya: FYI on commercial impacts if they push changes to order form liability or retention.

Cheers,
Jonas
Jonas Weber
Head of Legal Operations, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0129

[attachment: Redwood_DPA_redline_v3.docx] [attachment: OrderForm-commercial-markup.xlsx]

From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@cardiopath.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: legal@cardiopath.com, tom.ellis@cardiopath.com
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 13:45:00 +0000
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form: DPA execution playbook and SCCs / TIA coordination

Jonas —

Thanks for the draft. A couple of immediate items from our side after a quick read:

1) Role mapping: CardioPath expects Redwood to be Processor for all hosted inference services and recommends a narrow exhibit for Controller-only interactions (e.g., when Redwood enriches customer datasets). We can accept Redwood's proposed wording if you add a declarative exhibit listing the data flows.

2) TIA: we raised two commercial-conditioned mitigations in our comments — we attached CardioPath_DPA_comments_v1.docx with inline notes (see sections 4 and 6). Our privacy team wants a clearer statement on cross-border monitoring and the fallback mechanism if a transfer risk is identified.

3) Subprocessors: procurement requires a named list for execution (not just a published link). Please provide a snapshot of subprocessors as an exhibit.

4) Evidence: procurement needs SOC 2 + export control mitigations (short statement or schedule). Can your team provide a short evidence packet or a link to a certified SOC 2 report?

We will route the redlines through our legal lead this afternoon. Target for our counterredline is EOD 2026-12-02. If that slips we may request an extension on the signature deadline.

Best,
Elena
Elena Rossi
Head of Legal, CardioPath Analytics
elena.rossi@cardiopath.com

[attachment: CardioPath_DPA_comments_v1.docx]

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, monica.patel@redwood.ai
Cc: aditya.rao@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 09:08:00 +0000
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form: DPA execution playbook and SCCs / TIA coordination

Jonas / team —

I reviewed CardioPath's comments and Elena's note. Quick plan and proposed edits:

- I'll prepare an exhibit template for role mapping and a snapshot subprocessor list (to be updated automatically post-signature). That addresses their procurement requirement for a named list while preserving our operational flexibility.
- For the TIA: propose we keep the technical mitigations in the DPA and add an operational TIA schedule that summarizes export risk assessment + fallback (e.g., restrict routing to EU region, mandatory KMS customer-managed if requested). Draft attached: TIA-draft.pdf.
- Evidence packet: Monica, can you assemble the SOC 2 statement + short export-control mitigations summary by EOD 2026-12-02? We can link to the SOC 2 report in the Drive folder and include a one-page summary for procurement.
- Commercial redlines in order form: Aditya, if CardioPath pushes retention or liability changes we need a +/− margin to keep the deal economics intact. See OrderForm-commercial-markup.xlsx for suggested concession thresholds.

I'll produce a concise redline that accepts most of CardioPath's pragmatic wording but keeps our standard indemnity and deletion timelines. Once they return a counter, we can rapid-cycle to signature.

Laura Bennett
Sr. Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai

[attachment: TIA-draft.pdf]

From: CardioPath Legal <legal@cardiopath.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@cardiopath.com>, Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@cardiopath.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 16:22:00 +0000
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form: DPA execution playbook and SCCs / TIA coordination

Hi Jonas / Laura —

Thanks for the clarifications and the TIA draft. Our privacy lead confirmed the following after reviewing your TIA-draft.pdf and proposed exhibit approach:

- We can accept an exhibit snapshot for subprocessors provided it is explicitly versioned and we receive notification of material changes.
- We want the fallback operational flow to include a 5-business-day notice and written remediation plan from Redwood if a transfer risk is detected.
- A brief SOC 2 evidence summary will work for procurement; please provide as a PDF.

We have a few very small redlines in the controller/processor language (non-substantive clarifying edits). We will produce a marked-up DPA and, subject to those small edits and receipt of the SOC 2 summary, authorize DocuSign. Expect our counter by EOD 2026-12-02.

Please send the DocuSign template once we align text (we prefer to use our standard execution flow).

Regards,
CardioPath Legal Team
legal@cardiopath.com

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: legal@cardiopath.com, elena.rossi@cardiopath.com
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, monica.patel@redwood.ai, aditya.rao@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 3 Dec 2026 15:48:00 +0000
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form: DPA execution playbook and SCCs / TIA coordination

Great — thanks everyone. Quick summary and action items to keep us on the procurement gate timeline (EOD 2026-12-07):

1) Laura to finalize DPA redline accepting CardioPath's clarifying changes and adding the role exhibit (ETA: 2026-12-03 18:00 UTC).
2) Monica to upload SOC 2 summary + export-mitigations one-pager to Drive and share link (ETA: 2026-12-02 close of business — done). Drive link: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/Drive/Contracts/CardioPath/DPA/
3) Aditya to confirm commercial concession thresholds and confirm whether sales can approve the concession table (OrderForm-commercial-markup.xlsx) by 2026-12-04 12:00 UTC.
4) CardioPath to return final marked DPA; if only minor editorial changes remain, we will agree on DocuSign flow and execute.

Monica: I saw your SOC 2 upload and the TIA is in the Drive. Laura / Aditya — please confirm once you push the final files and I will coordinate execution with CardioPath legal.

Thanks — moving to FYI closed-loop: once signed we will append a short runbook for any future subprocessor additions and the notice workflow (we agreed a 5-business-day written remediation window).

Jonas
Jonas Weber
Head of Legal Operations, Redwood Inference
